title: At Which Position Does a Gray Code Word Appear?

concept.title: Undo "i xor (i shifted right by one)": every bit of the position is the XOR of all the higher bits of the word
body: The *Gray code* lists the non-negative integers in an order in which two neighbouring words differ in exactly one bit. The word at the position `i` (counting from 0) is `g(i) = i ^ (i >> 1)`. The first words are `0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7, 5, 4`: position 2 holds 3, position 3 holds 2, position 4 holds 6. Given a word `g`, at which **position** `i` does it stand? For `6 5 4 7` the positions are `4 6 7 5`.

Write the formula bit by bit. The top bit of `g` equals the top bit of `i`. Every other bit of `g` is `g_k = i_k ^ i_{k+1}` (the bit of `i` XOR the bit of `i` above it). Going from the **top** down we can solve this: `i_k = g_k ^ i_{k+1}`. Unrolling it, `i_k` is the XOR of the bits `g_k, g_{k+1}, g_{k+2}, ...` of the word, that is, **the XOR of all the bits of `g` at or above the position `k`**. In other words, `i` is the *prefix XOR* of the bits of `g` read from the top.

body.code:
i = 0
while g:
    i ^= g          # adds g, g >> 1, g >> 2, ... (all by XOR)
    g >>= 1
print(i)

body: The loop adds `g`, `g >> 1`, `g >> 2`, ... by XOR, and the bit `k` of that XOR is exactly the XOR of the bits of `g` at positions `k` and above. At most 60 iterations per question. The same loop is the inverse of the formula `i ^ (i >> 1)`, so `g(i)` for the found `i` gives back `g`.

statement: The Gray code lists the non-negative integers so that the word at the position `i` (from 0) is `i ^ (i >> 1)`. For each given word `g` print the position at which it appears.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of questions.
The second line has `q` numbers `g`, the words of the Gray code.
outputFormat: Print `q` numbers on one line, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The words 6, 5, 4, 7 stand at the positions 4, 6, 7, 5.

hints: g = i ^ (i >> 1), so each bit of g is a bit of i XOR the bit above it.
Solve from the top bit down: i_k = g_k ^ i_{k+1}.
The whole thing is the loop i ^= g; g >>= 1.

explanation: The position is the prefix XOR of the bits of the word read from the top; the loop that XORs g, g >> 1, g >> 2, ... computes it.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
gs = list(map(int, input().split()))

out = []
for g in gs:
    i = 0
    while g:
        i ^= g
        g >>= 1
    out.append(i)
print(*out)
